source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
The document lays out a standard corn growth timeline in weeks (week 1 through week 19) covering seed soaking through harvest:

Seed soaking (ចេញពន្លក / sprouting prep): weeks 1-2 (1-2 weeks).

Germination/vegetative growth (ចេញលូតលាស់): roughly weeks 3-9 (6-8 weeks) -- this is the plant's main stalk and leaf growth period.

Flowering (ចេញផ្កា): roughly weeks 10-11 (1-2 weeks) -- tasseling and silking occur here.

Grain filling / cob and kernel formation (ចេញផ្លែ/ដាក់គ្រាប់): roughly weeks 12-17 (8-10 weeks) -- the longest single stage, during which the ear fills out and kernels form and harden.

Drying and harvest (ទុំ/ប្រមូលផល): weeks 18-19 (1-2 weeks) -- the final stage where the crop dries down in the field before harvest.

Separately, the document notes farmers in mountainous/upland areas tend to plant in April and harvest in October (a roughly 6-month cycle counting land prep), farmers on flat lowland areas plant in June and harvest in September, and farmers in Pailin province plant in one wave and can harvest within a single year across three separate stagger-planted plots: a first planting harvested from May, a second from August, and a third harvested from November through December.
